issues.description: The template and problem statement use the label 'display_start' for the framebuffer base address (section .bss), but the solution's .bss declares 'screen_buffer' while the solution code still references 'display_start'. This name mismatch creates an undefined symbol in the solution and a structural inconsistency between template, solution, and problem statement, which will confuse students and break compilation if they compare or merge code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the framebuffer symbol name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the solution's 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start' in the .bss section, or update every reference to 'display_start' in the solution code to use 'screen_buffer'. Also ensure the problem statement and template use the same chosen name to avoid student confusion.

issues.description: The conceptual entity representing the start of the framebuffer is named inconsistently: the problem statement and the template use the symbol 'display_start', but the solution's BSS declares 'screen_buffer' (while other places in the same solution still reference 'display_start'). This mismatch between 'display_start' and 'screen_buffer' breaks the one-to-one mapping students expect between the problem description, the template, and the reference implementation and can cause confusion when locating the framebuffer base address.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the framebuffer base across all artifacts. For example, rename the BSS symbol in the solution from 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start' (or update the template/problem to use 'screen_buffer') and ensure all references in the solution use that same symbol name.
